<!--
INSTRUCTOR SETUP

This is a new companion lab. The original sampling.Rmd is unchanged.
It uses the same xaringan output, 16:9 ratio, split columns, incremental
reveals, minimal plot theme, and blue/orange palette as the sampling lab.
When available, it also uses ../slides.css and ../setup.Rmd. The supplied
reference did not include those two files. A standalone fallback is included.

RENDERING
Install the renderer once, if needed:
  install.packages(c("rmarkdown", "xaringan"))
Render from RStudio with Knit, or from R:
  rmarkdown::render("multitasking_lab.Rmd")
The setup chunk installs any missing analysis packages on your machine.

DATA OPTIONS
The default data_source is "demo": every analysis slide says SYNTHETIC DATA.
Set data_source to "csv" to read the local csv_file, or to "sheet" to read
sheet_url with googlesheets4. The sheet URL is deliberately blank: the M&M
sheet is not reused. Use a NEW sheet with these exact column headers:
  ID,Order,DS,DA,NS,NA
Each row represents one person. Order is 1, 2, 3, or 4. The four scores are
nonnegative integers. Blank means missing; zero means no correct numbers.
Copy those headers into a shared sheet or a CSV. A QR code appears when a
sheet_url is supplied and qrcode is installed. Otherwise share your normal
course link, or use the no-device board option on the data-entry slide.

The HTML contains a snapshot of the data at knit time, just like the sampling
lab's read_sheet workflow. After students enter their data, save/export the
CSV if using it, re-knit with data_source = "csv" or "sheet", reopen/refresh
the HTML, and jump to #class-results. No refresh occurs inside an open deck.
For the no-device option, enter rows in the CSV while students score, or
calculate four cell means on the board and use the interpretation slides.
If class-data loading fails, the deck displays a status message. It never
silently replaces unavailable class data with synthetic observations.

ACTIVITY LOGISTICS
Materials: paper and a pen per participant. Students draw their own four boxes.
No printing, special materials, student R installation, or individual timer.
Students use only one hand to write at a time. Use usual writing hand as D
and the other hand as N; these are task labels rather than a handedness test.
Students can be an observer/recorder if writing or speaking is inaccessible.
Students who observe take part in predictions, analysis, and the exit ticket.
With an odd class size, one trio rotates through writer/listener/recorder.
Each person still completes all four conditions. Allow two extra minutes
within the activity block and shorten the discussion if needed.

SCORING
Score is the last correctly completed number before the FIRST sequence error.
An omission, repetition, out-of-order number, or unreadable number ends the
correct prefix. An unfinished final number does not count. A visible correction
completed before time expires counts as corrected. Partners check afterward,
so the listener does not interrupt writing or coach during a trial.
Alphabet accuracy/rate is not a second numeric outcome. Partners note pauses
or abandoned recitation for discussion. Students prioritize both tasks and
recite continuously at a comfortable pace; no fixed alphabet rate is claimed.

ORDER
Use four sequences that balance condition positions and first-order carryover
across orders when equally represented: 1 = DS DA NA NS; 2 = DA NS DS NA;
3 = NS NA DA DS; 4 = NA DS NS DA. Actual classroom assignment may be uneven.
Number pairs 1-4 repeatedly. Partner A uses that order; B uses the next order,
wrapping 4 to 1. Each round slide lists the condition for every order.

PACING (50 MINUTES)
0-7: introduction, paper setup, scoring demonstration, predictions.
7-19: brief practice and all trials, both partners, including scoring.
19-24: entry, quick data checks, re-knit/jump to class results.
24-36: cell means, graph, main effects, simple effects, interaction.
36-45: interpretation, competing demands, design quality/variations.
45-50: exit ticket and wrap-up. Appendices are optional, outside this budget.

TIMERS
Each trial has an independent embedded 20-second timer: Start and Reset.
Timers require no internet or extra R package. They do not start automatically.
Click outside the timer before using slide-navigation keys. A timer ends with
a large STOP display; the instructor also announces stop. Reset before reuse.
If the display is unavailable, use one instructor stopwatch for the class.

NOTES
Press P in xaringan for presenter notes. Trial slides are generated by an R
helper so the eight timers and condition assignments stay consistent.
The analysis is descriptive. A nonzero sample difference in differences is
not a statistical test and is not labeled statistically significant.
-->

```{r course-setup, results='asis', echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Reuse the course setup when this file is in the same folder as sampling.Rmd.
# The standalone version can render without the unprovided course files.
if (file.exists("../setup.Rmd")) {
  cat(knitr::knit_child("../setup.Rmd", quiet = TRUE), sep = "\n")
}
```

```{r packages2, include=FALSE}
# Install-if-missing is intentional: this deck may be run on several machines.
needed <- c("ggplot2", "htmltools")
missing <- needed[!vapply(needed, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing)) install.packages(missing, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(ggplot2)
library(htmltools)
# xaringan::inf_mr(cast_from = "..")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                     out.width = "90%", fig.align = "center",
                     fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.3)

# Consistent palette + theme for all visuals, following the sampling deck.
base_cols <- c(Blue = "#0072CE", Orange = "#FF7F00")
thm <- theme_minimal(base_size = 17) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 8)),
        axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 8)),
        legend.position = "bottom")

# The order sequences balance positions and preceding conditions across orders.
orders <- rbind(c("DS", "DA", "NA", "NS"),
                c("DA", "NS", "DS", "NA"),
                c("NS", "NA", "DA", "DS"),
                c("NA", "DS", "NS", "DA"))
condition_labels <- c(DS = "Dominant + silent", DA = "Dominant + alphabet",
                      NS = "Non-dominant + silent", `NA` = "Non-dominant + alphabet")
score_cols <- c("DS", "DA", "NS", "NA")

# An iframe isolates each timer so its script runs inside a remark slide.
# The timer uses elapsed clock time, rather than assuming every tick is exact.
timer_widget <- function(seconds = 20) {
  timer_html <- paste0(
    '<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>',
    'body{margin:0;font-family:Arial,sans-serif;text-align:center;background:#f3f7fb;color:#17324d}',
    '#clock{font-size:62px;font-weight:bold;line-height:1.2;margin:5px}',
    'button{font-size:20px;padding:6px 22px;margin:0 8px;border:1px solid #0072CE;',
    'border-radius:5px;background:white;color:#17324d;cursor:pointer}',
    '</style></head><body><div id="clock" role="timer" aria-live="off">', seconds,
    '</div><button id="start">Start</button><button id="reset">Reset</button>',
    '<script>const duration=', seconds, ';let running=false,end=0,interval;',
    'const clock=document.getElementById("clock"),start=document.getElementById("start");',
    'function tick(){const left=Math.max(0,Math.ceil((end-performance.now())/1000));',
    'clock.textContent=left===0?"STOP":left;if(left===0){clearInterval(interval);',
    'running=false;clock.style.color="#b32025";start.disabled=true;}}',
    'start.onclick=function(){if(running)return;running=true;start.disabled=true;',
    'end=performance.now()+duration*1000;tick();interval=setInterval(tick,50);};',
    'document.getElementById("reset").onclick=function(){clearInterval(interval);',
    'running=false;clock.textContent=duration;clock.style.color="";start.disabled=false;};',
    '</script></body></html>'
  )
  as.character(tags$iframe(srcdoc = timer_html, title = "20-second class timer",
                          style = "width:100%;height:145px;border:0;", loading = "eager"))
}

# Every round uses the same scoring reminder and a fresh timer.
trial_slides <- function(partner) {
  for (round in seq_len(4)) {
    cat("\n\n---\n\n# Partner ", partner, ": round ", round, "\n\n", sep = "")
    cat("**Find your order number. Use the condition in your row.**\n\n")
    cat("| Your order | This round |\n|:--:|:--|\n")
    for (ord in seq_len(4)) {
      code <- orders[ord, round]
      cat("| ", ord, " | **", code, "**: ", condition_labels[[code]], " |\n", sep = "")
    }
    cat("\nWrite 1, 2, 3... in the matching box. Alphabet condition: say A-Z aloud, repeatedly.\n\n")
    cat(timer_widget(), "\n\n")
    cat("**After STOP:** check the sequence, circle your score, and record it in that box.\n\n")
    cat("???\nAllow about a minute for writing, scoring, and changing conditions. ")
    cat("Everyone starts at 1. Click outside the timer before advancing.\n")
  }
}
```

class: middle

# Can You Multitask?

## A factorial design challenge

Paper. Pen. Two tasks competing for your attention.

???
Start of the 0-7 minute introduction. Materials are ordinary paper and a pen.
No student computers or printing are required for the activity itself.

---

## Roadmap

- Setup and predictions (7 min)
- Hands-on challenge with a partner (12 min)
- Score entry and class-data check (5 min)
- Class analysis: four cells, main effects, interaction (12 min)
- Interpretation and study design (9 min)
- Exit ticket and wrap-up (5 min)

--

**By the end, you should be able to explain what a difference in differences means using your own data.**

---

# The challenge

.pull-left[
**Task 1: write numbers**

Write 1, 2, 3, 4... for 20 seconds.

Sometimes use your usual writing hand.

Sometimes use your other hand.
]

.pull-right[
**Task 2: say the alphabet**

In some rounds, write in silence.

In other rounds, say A-Z aloud while you write.

Keep repeating the alphabet until time ends.
]

???
Demonstrate writing while saying the alphabet for a few seconds. A writer
does not sing, whisper silently, or switch to saying the written numbers.
The listener should hear the alphabet. All alphabet writers will be audible
at once. Mention that classroom noise is a limitation, not controlled silence.

---

# Two factors, four conditions

| | Silent | Alphabet aloud |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **Dominant hand** | **DS** | **DA** |
| **Non-dominant hand** | **NS** | **NA** |

- **D:** your usual writing hand. **N:** your other hand.
- Every participant completes all four conditions.
- Each round lasts **20 seconds**.

--

**Does adding the alphabet affect writing equally with both hands?**

---

# Paper setup

.pull-left[
Divide your paper into four boxes.

Label them **DS, DA, NS, NA**.

Leave room to write several rows of numbers in each box.

Add your participant code and order number at the top.
]

.pull-right[
| DS | DA |
|:--:|:--:|
| Dominant + silent | Dominant + alphabet |
| **NS** | **NA** |
| Non-dominant + silent | Non-dominant + alphabet |

You will record **one score per box**.
]

???
Pair codes can be pair01A and pair01B. Avoid student names in projected data.
An observer role is available without requiring a student to explain why.

---

# What counts as the score?

Your score is the **last correctly completed number before the first sequence error**.

.score-example[1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8]

**Score = 4.** The sequence first goes wrong when 5 is skipped.

--

- A repeated, out-of-order, or unreadable number also ends the correct sequence.
- An unfinished final number does not count.
- A correction completed before STOP counts as corrected.
- Keep writing during the round. Check and circle the score afterward.

???
Ask for the score before revealing it. If no number is correct, score 0.
This measure combines speed with sequence accuracy. It is not a pure measure
of writing speed. Do not add an arbitrary time or error penalty.

---

# Partner roles

.pull-left[
**Writer**

- Start each round at 1.
- Use the assigned hand.
- Keep the same pen and paper position.
- In alphabet rounds, keep both tasks going at a comfortable pace.
]

.pull-right[
**Listener / recorder**

- Check the assigned condition.
- Listen during alphabet rounds.
- After STOP, check the number sequence with the writer.
- Note any long alphabet pauses for discussion.
]

**Both tasks matter.** Keep going after an alphabet slip and return to the alphabet.

???
Listeners do not count alphabet errors or police a particular rate. Those
would add recording demands. They do not interrupt or coach the writer.
The instructor runs one timer for everyone.

---

# Your order number

Count pairs **1, 2, 3, 4**, then repeat.

- Partner A uses the pair's number as their order.
- Partner B uses the next order: **1 becomes 2, 2 becomes 3, 3 becomes 4, 4 becomes 1**.

.small[
| Order | Round 1 | Round 2 | Round 3 | Round 4 |
|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| 1 | DS | DA | NA | NS |
| 2 | DA | NS | DS | NA |
| 3 | NS | NA | DA | DS |
| 4 | NA | DS | NS | DA |
]

**Each round slide shows you what to do.**

???
These orders spread practice, fatigue, and preceding conditions across the
four conditions. Equal order-group sizes would balance them exactly; the
class may be uneven. The shared room remains an imperfect noise control.

---

# Your prediction

With your partner:

1. Which condition will have the highest writing score?
2. Will saying the alphabet reduce scores equally with both hands?
3. What result would make you change your mind?

--

Write one sentence: **"We predict the alphabet will have a larger effect when..."**

???
Keep predictions to about a minute. Students may predict that the familiar
motor task leaves more capacity for the alphabet, or a different pattern.
Do not promise that the class will show a particular interaction.

---

# Quick practice

- Both partners: write a few numbers with each hand in a margin.
- Try writing while saying **A, B, C, D...** aloud for a few seconds.
- Check that both partners understand the score.

**Practice stays in the margin. The four labeled boxes are for the timed rounds.**

Partner A writes first. Partner B listens and checks the score.

???
Start the 7-19 minute activity block. Keep practice under a minute.
Practice is informal and unscored; it is not another experimental condition.

```{r partner-a-rounds, results='asis'}
trial_slides("A")
```

---

# Switch roles

Partner A: confirm that **all four boxes have a circled score**.

Partner B: use your own four boxes and your own order number.

- Pair order 1: Partner B uses **2**.
- Pair order 2: Partner B uses **3**.
- Pair order 3: Partner B uses **4**.
- Pair order 4: Partner B uses **1**.

**Partner B writes. Partner A listens and checks.**

```{r partner-b-rounds, results='asis'}
trial_slides("B")
```

---

# Four scores per person

Before entering your data:

- Check the score against each written sequence.
- Match each score to **DS, DA, NS, or NA**, regardless of trial order.
- Keep **0** if no number was correct. Leave a missed condition blank.
- Use a participant code. Enter one row per person.

.small[
| ID | Order | DS | DA | NS | NA |
|:--|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| pair01A | 1 | Your score | Your score | Your score | Your score |
]

???
Start the 19-24 minute entry block. ID must be unique. Order means the
individual's order number, not necessarily the pair number.

---

# Data collection

.pull-left[
```{r data-link, results='asis'}
if (nzchar(trimws(params$sheet_url))) {
  cat(as.character(tags$p(tags$a(href = params$sheet_url,
                                "Open the class data sheet", target = "_blank"))))
  if (requireNamespace("qrcode", quietly = TRUE)) {
    plot(qrcode::qr_code(params$sheet_url))
  } else {
    cat("\nUse the class link shared by your instructor.\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("**Use the data-entry link shared by your instructor.**\n\n")
  cat("No devices? Read your four scores to the recorder for the class table.\n")
}
```
]

.pull-right[
**Headers**

`ID, Order, DS, DA, NS, NA`

**While entries arrive:**

- Did any round feel easier than you expected?
- Did the alphabet slow down when writing got harder?
- What happened to the room's noise level?
]

???
For the board option, record one row per participant under the six headers.
If data entry is slow, calculate column means from the board and continue
with the interpretation prompts. Synthetic slides must remain labeled.
Re-knit class-data mode after entries arrive, refresh the HTML, and jump to
#class-results. Knitting does not update an already open HTML automatically.

```{r analysis-data, include=FALSE}
# Read class data explicitly. Never switch to demo data after a class-data error.
source_mode <- tolower(trimws(params$data_source))
load_message <- ""
raw <- data.frame()
if (identical(source_mode, "demo")) {
  # Synthetic observations demonstrate an interaction; they are not predictions.
  # Shared person effects retain the repeated-measures structure in the example.
  set.seed(210)
  person <- rnorm(24, 0, 3)
  raw <- data.frame(
    ID = sprintf("demo%02d", seq_len(24)), Order = rep(1:4, 6),
    DS = pmax(0, round(42 + person + rnorm(24, 0, 2))),
    DA = pmax(0, round(35 + person + rnorm(24, 0, 2))),
    NS = pmax(0, round(28 + person + rnorm(24, 0, 2))),
    `NA` = pmax(0, round(14 + person + rnorm(24, 0, 2))),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
} else if (source_mode %in% c("csv", "sheet")) {
  raw <- tryCatch({
    if (source_mode == "csv") {
      read.csv(params$csv_file, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    } else {
      if (!nzchar(trimws(params$sheet_url))) stop("Set sheet_url before using sheet mode.")
      if (!requireNamespace("googlesheets4", quietly = TRUE)) {
        install.packages("googlesheets4", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
      }
      # Use your usual signed-in session for private sheets; public sheets can
      # instead use googlesheets4::gs4_deauth() before rendering if preferred.
      as.data.frame(googlesheets4::read_sheet(params$sheet_url))
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    load_message <<- paste("Class data could not be loaded:", conditionMessage(e))
    data.frame()
  })
} else {
  load_message <- "Choose data_source = demo, csv, or sheet in the YAML settings."
}

# Require one unique person and four valid scores for every comparison.
# Using the same complete participants in all cells preserves paired contrasts.
n_raw <- nrow(raw)
n_excluded <- 0L
df <- data.frame()
required <- c("ID", "Order", score_cols)
if (n_raw > 0 && !all(required %in% names(raw))) {
  load_message <- paste("Missing columns:", paste(setdiff(required, names(raw)), collapse = ", "))
} else if (n_raw > 0) {
  raw <- raw[, required, drop = FALSE]
  raw$ID <- trimws(as.character(raw$ID))
  # Exclude every copy of a duplicated ID rather than picking one silently.
  duplicate_id <- duplicated(raw$ID) | duplicated(raw$ID, fromLast = TRUE)
  for (nm in score_cols) raw[[nm]] <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(raw[[nm]])))
  score_matrix <- as.matrix(raw[, score_cols, drop = FALSE])
  valid_scores <- apply(score_matrix, 1, function(x) {
    all(is.finite(x) & x >= 0 & x == floor(x))
  })
  valid_id <- !is.na(raw$ID) & nzchar(raw$ID) & !duplicate_id
  df <- raw[valid_scores & valid_id, , drop = FALSE]
  n_excluded <- n_raw - nrow(df)
}
has_data <- nrow(df) > 0
data_label <- if (source_mode == "demo") "SYNTHETIC DATA: example only" else "CLASS DATA: snapshot at render time"
if (!has_data && !nzchar(load_message)) load_message <- "Waiting for complete, valid participant rows."
data_banner <- function() {
  detail <- if (has_data) {
    paste0(nrow(df), " complete participants; ", n_excluded, " rows excluded.")
  } else load_message
  cat(as.character(tags$div(class = "data-banner", data_label, tags$br(), detail)))
}
no_data <- function() cat("\n**No class results to display yet.** Use the table and prompts to discuss your board results.\n")

if (has_data) {
  # Build long-format data without treating the four rows as independent people.
  df_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(score_cols, function(code) {
    data.frame(ID = df$ID, Condition = code,
               Hand = if (substr(code, 1, 1) == "D") "Dominant" else "Non-dominant",
               Task = if (substr(code, 2, 2) == "S") "Silent" else "Alphabet",
               Score = df[[code]])
  }))
  df_long$Hand <- factor(df_long$Hand, levels = c("Dominant", "Non-dominant"))
  df_long$Task <- factor(df_long$Task, levels = c("Silent", "Alphabet"))
  cell_means <- aggregate(Score ~ Hand + Task, df_long, mean)
  mu <- colMeans(df[, score_cols, drop = FALSE])
  dominant_mean <- mean(mu[c("DS", "DA")])
  nondominant_mean <- mean(mu[c("NS", "NA")])
  silent_mean <- mean(mu[c("DS", "NS")])
  alphabet_mean <- mean(mu[c("DA", "NA")])
  # Define all alphabet costs as silent minus alphabet. Positive = lower score
  # with the alphabet. Interaction is non-dominant cost minus dominant cost.
  df$Cost_D <- df$DS - df$DA
  df$Cost_N <- df$NS - df[["NA"]]
  df$Interaction <- df$Cost_N - df$Cost_D
  interaction_mean <- mean(df$Interaction)
}
```

---
name: class-results

# Our four cell means

```{r results-banner, results='asis'}
data_banner()
```

```{r cell-table, results='asis'}
if (has_data) {
  tab <- data.frame(Hand = c("Dominant", "Non-dominant", "Task mean"),
                    Silent = c(mu["DS"], mu["NS"], silent_mean),
                    Alphabet = c(mu["DA"], mu["NA"], alphabet_mean),
                    `Hand mean` = c(dominant_mean, nondominant_mean, mean(mu)),
                    check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
  cat(knitr::kable(tab, format = "html", digits = 1, row.names = FALSE))
} else no_data()
```

**Outcome:** correct consecutive numbers written in 20 seconds.

Higher scores indicate more correct output.

???
Start the 24-36 minute analysis block. Use the same complete participants for
all four means. Marginal means give equal weight to the two conditions.
The synthetic case is only a worked example; class results can differ.

---

# What does the interaction plot show?

```{r graph-banner, results='asis'}
data_banner()
```

```{r interaction-plot, results='asis', out.width='82%'}
if (has_data) {
  print(ggplot(cell_means, aes(Task, Score, color = Hand, group = Hand)) +
          geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) + geom_point(size = 3.5) +
          scale_color_manual(values = unname(base_cols)) +
          scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .08))) +
          labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean correct consecutive numbers", color = "Writing hand") + thm)
} else no_data()
```

**Compare the changes from silent to alphabet for the two hands.**

???
Ask students to describe each line first, then compare slopes. A crossover
is not required for an interaction. No inferential uncertainty is shown.

---

# Main effect: writing hand

Average across the silent and alphabet conditions for each hand.

```{r hand-main-effect, results='asis'}
data_banner()
if (has_data) {
  cat(sprintf("\n\n**Dominant:** (%.1f + %.1f) / 2 = **%.1f**\n\n",
              mu["DS"], mu["DA"], dominant_mean))
  cat(sprintf("**Non-dominant:** (%.1f + %.1f) / 2 = **%.1f**\n\n",
              mu["NS"], mu["NA"], nondominant_mean))
  cat(sprintf("**Dominant minus non-dominant = %.1f numbers.**\n", dominant_mean - nondominant_mean))
} else no_data()
```

**Question:** Averaging across the two tasks, how do the hands differ?

---

# Main effect: adding the alphabet

Average across the dominant and non-dominant hands for each task.

```{r task-main-effect, results='asis'}
data_banner()
if (has_data) {
  cat(sprintf("\n\n**Silent:** (%.1f + %.1f) / 2 = **%.1f**\n\n",
              mu["DS"], mu["NS"], silent_mean))
  cat(sprintf("**Alphabet:** (%.1f + %.1f) / 2 = **%.1f**\n\n",
              mu["DA"], mu["NA"], alphabet_mean))
  cat(sprintf("**Silent minus alphabet = %.1f numbers.**\n", silent_mean - alphabet_mean))
} else no_data()
```

**Question:** Averaging across hands, how does adding the alphabet affect output?

---

# Two simple effects

Calculate the **alphabet cost** separately for each hand:

**Silent score minus alphabet score.** Positive values mean lower output with the alphabet.

```{r simple-effects, results='asis'}
data_banner()
if (has_data) {
  tab <- data.frame(Hand = c("Dominant", "Non-dominant"),
                    Silent = c(mu["DS"], mu["NS"]),
                    Alphabet = c(mu["DA"], mu["NA"]),
                    `Alphabet cost` = c(mean(df$Cost_D), mean(df$Cost_N)),
                    check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
  cat(knitr::kable(tab, format = "html", digits = 1, row.names = FALSE))
} else no_data()
```

**Are these two costs similar, or does one look larger?**

---

# Interaction: a difference in differences

**Non-dominant alphabet cost minus dominant alphabet cost.**

```{r difference-in-differences, results='asis'}
data_banner()
if (has_data) {
  cat(sprintf("\n\n(%.1f - %.1f) - (%.1f - %.1f) = **%.1f numbers**\n\n",
              mu["NS"], mu["NA"], mu["DS"], mu["DA"], interaction_mean))
}
```

- **Positive:** a larger alphabet cost with the non-dominant hand.
- **Negative:** a larger alphabet cost with the dominant hand.
- **Zero:** the same alphabet cost with both hands.

**A sample difference describes our data. A statistical test would address uncertainty.**

???
Do not equate any nonzero number or visibly nonparallel lines with a
statistically supported interaction. Keep all signs consistent with the
silent-minus-alphabet definition. Round only for display.

---

# Describe what happened

With your partner, complete these sentences using the class results:

1. "Averaging across tasks, output was..."
2. "Averaging across hands, adding the alphabet..."
3. "The alphabet cost was ___ for the dominant hand and ___ for the other hand."
4. "This suggests that the effect of adding the alphabet..."

--

**Which sentence answers the interaction question?**

???
Begin the 36-45 minute interpretation block. Sentence 4 should compare
the two simple effects, rather than naming only the easiest/hardest cell.

---

# Did everyone show the same pattern?

```{r people-banner, results='asis'}
data_banner()
```

```{r individual-contrasts, results='asis', out.width='80%'}
if (has_data) {
  print(ggplot(df, aes(x = Interaction)) +
          geom_dotplot(binwidth = 1, dotsize = .65, stackdir = "up",
                       fill = base_cols[["Blue"]], color = "white") +
          geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#555555") +
          labs(x = "Non-dominant cost minus dominant cost", y = NULL) +
          thm + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank()))
} else no_data()
```

The class average can hide differences among people.

???
Each dot is one participant's paired difference in differences. This is
not four independent samples. Avoid attributing person differences to a
specific trait without measuring it. Skip this slide if behind schedule.

---

# What did you do when the task got harder?

.pull-left[
**Writer's experience**

- Did you slow your writing?
- Did you slow the alphabet?
- Did you stop one task to keep the other going?
]

.pull-right[
**Listener's observations**

- Did recitation pause?
- Were there number-sequence errors?
- Did performance change with practice?
]

**We measured writing output. We did not measure both tasks equally.**

???
This is a task-priority limitation. A future study could record alphabet
rate and accuracy, but that would need more measurement than today's lab.

---

# How strong is our design?

.pull-left[
**Features that help**

- Each person is their own comparison.
- Every round has the same duration.
- Everyone restarts the same number sequence.
- Orders spread practice and fatigue across conditions.
]

.pull-right[
**Limits to discuss**

- The room was not silent when others recited.
- Alphabet pace could vary across rounds.
- Our score combines speed and sequence accuracy.
- One short trial per cell leaves measurement noise.
]

???
Distinguish intended silence (no self-recitation) from an acoustically quiet
room. Other pairs can be speaking during a silent condition. Do not claim
fully isolated experimental conditions. Hand assignment is a manipulation
of the hand used, not random assignment of a handedness trait.

---

# Same question, different designs

| Design | What each participant does |
|:--|:--|
| **Within-groups: today's design** | All four hand/task combinations |
| **Between-groups** | One randomly assigned hand/task combination |
| **Mixed** | One assigned hand, both task conditions |

With your partner: **Which design reduces practice across conditions? Which makes person-to-person differences harder to control?**

???
The mixed example assigns which hand to use between people, while task is
within people. With the same number per cell, between-groups needs more
participants than the all-within design. No new data collection is needed.
Skip detailed factorial extensions if the class is near minute 45.

---

# Exit ticket

Answer individually:

1. Give the factorial notation and identify which factors are within-groups.
2. Use the four class cell means to calculate the difference in differences.
3. Describe that result in one sentence about **how the alphabet effect depends on hand**.
4. Identify one design limitation and a specific change that would address it.

???
Start the 45-50 minute exit/wrap-up block. Expected design: 2 x 2, both
factors within-groups. For item 2, use (NS - NA) - (DS - DA). Accept a
reversed sign when the student defines and interprets it consistently.
No interaction in class data is a valid outcome to explain.

---

# Wrapping up...

.pull-left[
## What our four cells tell us

- A main effect averages across the other factor.
- A simple effect examines one level of the other factor.
- An interaction compares those simple effects.
]

.pull-right[
## Our central question

**Does adding a second task affect writing equally with both hands?**

The answer comes from a **difference in differences**.
]

???
End of the 50-minute lab. The remaining slides are optional references.

---
class: middle

# Optional reference slides

Outside the 50-minute activity

---

# A worked example

**Invented means for arithmetic practice.**

| | Silent | Alphabet | Hand mean |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| Dominant | 40 | 34 | 37 |
| Non-dominant | 26 | 12 | 19 |
| Task mean | 33 | 23 | 28 |

- Main effect of hand: **37 - 19 = 18**.
- Main effect of task: **33 - 23 = 10**.
- Interaction: **(26 - 12) - (40 - 34) = 8**.

The alphabet cost is 8 numbers larger with the non-dominant hand.

---

# An interaction does not require crossing lines

```{r optional-patterns, fig.height=4.2, out.width='90%'}
examples <- data.frame(
  Pattern = rep(c("Equal costs", "Different costs"), each = 4),
  Hand = rep(rep(c("Dominant", "Non-dominant"), each = 2), 2),
  Task = rep(c("Silent", "Alphabet"), 4),
  Score = c(40, 32, 26, 18, 40, 34, 26, 12)
)
examples$Task <- factor(examples$Task, levels = c("Silent", "Alphabet"))
examples$Hand <- factor(examples$Hand, levels = c("Dominant", "Non-dominant"))
ggplot(examples, aes(Task, Score, color = Hand, group = Hand)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) + geom_point(size = 3) + facet_wrap(~ Pattern) +
  scale_color_manual(values = unname(base_cols)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 45)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Correct consecutive numbers", color = "Writing hand") + thm
```

**Invented examples. Compare the slopes, not whether the lines cross.**

---

# A third factor?

Imagine adding **practice: before versus after a practice session**.

- Design: **2 x 2 x 2**.
- Eight combinations of hand, task, and practice.
- Three-way question: **Does practice change the hand-by-task interaction?**

We would compare the difference in differences before and after practice.

???
Connect to the deck's three-way interactions. Merely testing before and
after does not isolate a causal practice effect from time and retesting.
A control group or other design changes would strengthen that inference.

---

# Analysis code: the paired comparisons

.small[
```{r show-analysis, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
# One row per person, with the same complete people in all four conditions.
mu <- colMeans(df[, c("DS", "DA", "NS", "NA")])

# Marginal differences.
hand_effect <- mean(mu[c("DS", "DA")]) - mean(mu[c("NS", "NA")])
task_effect <- mean(mu[c("DS", "NS")]) - mean(mu[c("DA", "NA")])

# Individual alphabet costs, then the individual difference in differences.
df$Cost_D <- df$DS - df$DA
df$Cost_N <- df$NS - df[["NA"]]
df$Interaction <- df$Cost_N - df$Cost_D

# Mean of paired contrasts equals the contrast of the four cell means.
mean(df$Interaction)
(mu["NS"] - mu["NA"]) - (mu["DS"] - mu["DA"])
```
]
